transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE, and Devon's my SE. Goal today is to run through your security posture and see which deployment mode makes sense.
[00:12] Ellen Park: Hi Maya, hi Devon. Ellen here, head of security at Sapphire. Marcus and Samir are on as well. We've got a pretty strict compliance bar — SOC2 Type II in place, working toward ISO, and we need to understand log/retention and key management.
[00:27] Marcus Varela: Hi all. From CTO side, main ask is that any PII never leaves our control and key usage is auditable.
[00:36] Devon Ortiz: Great, thanks. Can you walk me through where your model-hosted data would live — are you comfortable with a hosted SaaS where we handle keys, or do you require BYOK/HSM and private deployment?
[00:48] Samir Patel: For production, we prefer BYOK. For an initial eval maybe hosted is ok but only if we can enforce strict retention and we can export logs to our Splunk.
[00:59] Ellen Park: Also need SSO — Okta — and SCIM provisioning, plus RBAC at the route/model level.
[01:08] Maya Chen: Understood. We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. For RBAC, we have role tiers and route-level policies; I'll let Devon explain granularity.
[01:20] Devon Ortiz: Right. We expose RBAC that maps to roles — admin, engineer, viewer — and you can scope policies per-model, per-route. There's also token-level auditing so you can see which API key made requests. Caveat: in Hosted we manage the master key unless you opt for BYOK via KMS. In Dedicated and Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM.
[01:47] Ellen Park: When you say KMS, is it cloud KMS or do you support customer HSM appliances?
[01:53] Devon Ortiz: Both. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) and we have integrations for external HSMs in Private deployments. There's an HSM-backed BYOK flow for on-prem or VPC Private.
[02:07] Marcus Varela: Nice. What's the audit trail look like? We need immutable logs for access to keys and to model outputs tied to user principals.
[02:16] Devon Ortiz: We emit audit logs for auth events, key ops, model inference requests (metadata only — not full prompt by default unless you enable full logging). Logs can be retained per org and we support log forwarding to your SIEM via syslog/S3 ingestion. Retention policies can be configured; default is 90 days in Hosted, but Dedicated/Private you can set longer retention.
[02:40] Samir Patel: Does Redwood keep KV cache or prompt cache by default? We want to ensure caches are not persisted beyond retention.
[02:47] Devon Ortiz: Good question. We have prefix/KV caching optimizations. In Hosted, caching is ephemeral and we can disable cross-tenant caching; you can configure cache TTL and whether it's persisted. For Private, you control cache persistence.
[02:58] Ellen Park: SOC2 artifacts — do you provide the Type II report and the control matrix?
[03:03] Maya Chen: Yes, we can share our SOC2 Type II report and a control mapping. I'll attach the compliance pack after this call.
[03:10] Marcus Varela: We're also ISO-curious. What's in scope for your ISO 27001?
[03:15] Maya Chen: Our ISO scope covers the inference platform, console, and control plane services — I'll include the scope statement.
[03:22] Ellen Park: On SSO, we need SAML and SCIM for user provisioning. Are there any known limitations like group sync?
[03:29] Devon Ortiz: We support SAML for auth and SCIM for provisioning with group sync. There's also Okta best-practice docs we'll share. Occasionally the auto-provision mapping needs tweaks for custom groups — it's pretty standard.
[03:41] Ellen Park: RBAC — can we create roles for canary teams and limit model rollouts? We want to ensure only certain principals can change rollout policies.
[03:50] Devon Ortiz: Yes — RBAC policy can target rollout controls. You can separate 'deploy' from 'invoke' permissions. There was, uh, a previous mislabel in some older console versions where 'edit' encompassed both; that was fixed in the last release, but I'll confirm the seat-level enforcement.
[04:07] Marcus Varela: Good. Another question: data residency in EU — we have EU customers and data must remain in eu-west-1. How do you guarantee region-scope?
[04:16] Maya Chen: We can pin workloads to regions; for Hosted we have region isolation. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployed within your VPC in that region.
[04:26] Samir Patel: For Private deployment, what's the network model — do you funnel traffic through your control plane? Concerned about metadata leaving our VPC.
[04:34] Devon Ortiz: In Private, the control plane can be customer-hosted or we provide a minimal control channel; you can opt for air-gapped on-prem where the control plane is entirely internal. For standard Private, there's a customer-managed control plane which reduces metadata egress. We'll diagram the flows in the deep-dive.
[04:50] Ellen Park: Encryption at rest — do you support per-tenant keys?
[04:54] Devon Ortiz: Yes, per-tenant encryption keys via KMS. We support envelope encryption and KMS CMKs. For extra assurance, HSM-backed keys and key rotation policies are available.
[05:04] Marcus Varela: About logs — do you keep request/response payloads? That's sensitive.
[05:09] Devon Ortiz: By default we do not persist full request/response payloads for Hosted production; metadata and tokens only. If you enable full request logging for debug/quality monitoring, those can be routed to your SIEM with encryption, or stored in a customer-owned S3 for Private/Dedicated.
[05:26] Ellen Park: Is there a way to scrub PII automatically before logs are retained?
[05:31] Devon Ortiz: We have an optional PII redaction pipeline and tokenization features; typically part of Redwood Optimize/quality flows but can be enabled as a logging preprocessor. I'll include the redaction doc.
[05:42] Samir Patel: For billing and cost attribution, we want token-level cost breakdowns tied to teams. Does audit logging capture token usage per API key?
[05:50] Maya Chen: Yes — our console provides token-level cost and you can map API keys to teams; audit logs show per-key usage.
[05:58] Ellen Park: Any third-party sub-processors we should be aware of?
[06:01] Maya Chen: We list sub-processors in the compliance pack, includes cloud providers and some infra vendors. We can provide the current list.
[06:08] Marcus Varela: About the POC — timeline? We'd like a short POC with real traffic and Splunk integration.
[06:14] Maya Chen: Typical POC is 4 weeks. If you need private deployment for the POC (to validate KMS & logs) we can stand up a Dedicated or Private environment; that will take slightly longer for infra.
[06:26] Samir Patel: What's the approximate lead time for Private on-prem?
[06:29] Devon Ortiz: On-prem air-gapped is the longest — typically 6–10 weeks depending on coordination. Private in your VPC with customer-managed KMS is 2–4 weeks. Dedicated (Redwood-managed infra reserved for you) is often 2–3 weeks.
[06:42] Ellen Park: For contractual safeguards, do you offer SOC2 attestation, DPA, and breach notification timelines?
[06:49] Maya Chen: Yes — DPA with standard 72-hour breach notification clauses we can negotiate. SOC2 attestation will be in the pack.
[06:58] Marcus Varela: Any caveats around model pinning and rollouts interfering with audit trails? We need an immutable record of which model served which request.
[07:06] Devon Ortiz: We store model version metadata with each inference event in the audit logs. You can pin models per route; the logs will reflect the model_id and deployed version.
[07:16] Ellen Park: Response time — sometimes we store outputs that could be considered sensitive. Can we ensure outputs are encrypted and accessible only to certain roles?
[07:25] Devon Ortiz: Yes, encryption at rest and ACLs on stored artifacts; plus RBAC to limit read access. For Hosted, we hold keys unless BYOK is enabled; with BYOK, you keep ultimate control.
[07:36] Samir Patel: A few practical asks for the follow-up deep-dive: network diagram, KMS key lifecycle, sample audit log with redaction, and example policy definitions for RBAC.
[07:47] Maya Chen: We'll deliver those. Devon, anything else to surface?
[07:50] Devon Ortiz: I'll add some details on the SCIM mapping quirks we've seen and include a sample SIEM ingestion config for Splunk. Also I'll bring a short checklist for Private vs Dedicated migration steps.
[08:03] Ellen Park: Great. One last quick question: SLA for Dedicated/Private and telemetry retention differences?
[08:10] Maya Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; Private SLAs depend on deployment model and contract. Telemetry retention is configurable in Dedicated/Private; Hosted has default tiers. We'll add an explicit table in the follow-up.
[08:25] Marcus Varela: Ok that sounds good. Let's reconvene after you send the SOC2 and the architecture docs.
[08:30] Maya Chen: Perfect — we'll email the compliance pack and propose times for the technical deep-dive week of Nov 8. Thanks everyone.
[08:36] Ellen Park: Thanks — appreciate the thoroughness.
[08:38] Samir Patel: Thanks all.
[08:40] End of recording.
